summary: Frontend-only e2e testing of a single-page Household Budget app. Covered all 13 requested scenarios: render, editable labels, income, individual expenses (add/edit/reassign), household expenses (add/edit/delete), savings, emergency fund, positive & negative remaining coloring, currency toggle, localStorage persistence, and Reset. All 13 scenarios PASS functionally. Six initial test assertions on person-label rename appeared to fail (got 'ALEX' vs expected 'Alex') but were verified as CSS text-transform: uppercase (from the wrapping `.text-xs uppercase tracking-widest` container in EditableLabel host). Actual DOM textContent and localStorage store the correct casing ('Alex', 'Blair', 'Person A', 'Person B'). No real bugs found.

issues: Person label chip container applies CSS `uppercase` (text-transform) — labels always render in ALL CAPS regardless of the user's typed casing. Cosmetic only; DOM/localStorage keep correct case. Consider removing `uppercase` if the design intent was to preserve user casing (since the label is a display of the user-entered name).

action_items: OPTIONAL: reconsider CSS `uppercase` on the wrapping div of `person-a-label` / `person-b-label` in BudgetApp.jsx (the surrounding `<div class="mb-2 text-xs uppercase tracking-widest ...">`). It uppercases user-typed names visually. Not a functional bug — subtotal labels and add-button labels are NOT uppercased and correctly show the case the user typed.
critical_code_review_comments: BudgetApp.jsx is 730+ lines including small subcomponents (SummaryStat, RecapCell, NamedAmountRow, Section, SubtotalRow). Consider splitting subcomponents into their own files under components/budget/ for maintainability.
uid() uses Date.now + Math.random — fine for local-only IDs but could collide under rapid programmatic adds; consider crypto.randomUUID() when available.

EditableLabel: on empty blur it resets DOM text to old value via direct textContent mutation which bypasses React reconciliation; acceptable here because parent state didn't change, but fragile if surrounding text ever becomes dynamic.
useLocalStorage writes on every state change (including initial hydrate). Minor: potential quota churn; acceptable for this app size.
context_for_next_testing_agent: All feature-level test scenarios in the review request pass. If retesting, note that person-a-label / person-b-label render visually UPPERCASE due to CSS text-transform on the wrapping container — use `textContent` (or the localStorage value) rather than Playwright's `inner_text` when asserting stored/entered casing. Add-button labels and subtotal labels correctly reflect the actual user-entered casing.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. The apparent 6 failing assertions were a test-side artifact: Playwright's `inner_text` returns text with CSS `text-transform: uppercase` applied, whereas the actual React state and DOM `textContent` retain the exact case typed. Verified via localStorage inspection ('people':{'a':'Person A','b':'Person B'}) and `element.textContent`.
